name: Identify countries on a blank world map
blurb: All 195 countries is genuinely achievable in a month with spaced repetition, and it quietly improves how you read every news story thereafter.
gear: A map quiz site or app
steps: Learn region by region rather than alphabetically: Europe, then South America, then Africa, then Asia, then Oceania and the Caribbean.
Learn each region’s shape as a whole first, then place countries within it by their neighbours.
Use spaced repetition daily rather than cramming — this is exactly the kind of material it is built for.
Attack the hard clusters deliberately: West Africa, the Balkans, Central Asia and the Caribbean islands are where everyone loses points.
Draw blank maps from memory once a week, which is far harder and far more effective than clicking.
Add capitals and flags afterwards, once the locations are solid.
tips: Anchor unfamiliar countries to familiar neighbours rather than learning them in isolation.
Ten minutes daily beats two hours weekly by a wide margin for this kind of memorisation.
proof: You place all 195 countries correctly on a blank map quiz, in one sitting.
